newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on China rumors, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on China rumors, weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures posted double-digit gains on Wednesday on persistent rumors China was in the market for soybeans and on forecasts for rain and snow in key U.S. growing regions, traders said.
"With China around and the weather, we're going to bounce," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "We're hearing (China) bought 50,000 (tonnes) soybeans and are looking for another 50,000."
Meteorologists forecast two days of dry weather in the western Corn Belt before another round of showers soaked already-wet corn and soybean fields.

November tested the $7.00 mark and peaked briefly at $6.99-1/2 per bushel, the highest point since Oct 11 when soybean futures dropped the 30-cent limit after USDA raised its production estimate to 2.346 billion bushels.
But November/July spreads widened with July gaining 4-1/2 cents per bushel as U.S. Gulf CIF values fell, traders said.
Technically, a close above $6.95 per bushel in the November signaled a higher opening Thursday. Traders pegged resistance at $7.00-1/4 per bushel.
The market was anticipating another strong U.S. soybean export figure in Thursday's USDA export report.
"If the exports aren't there, we may not go anywhere on the open," a trader said. "We'll hit stops above $7.00. If we don't take them out early, we'll have trouble closing firm."
Soybeans ended nine to 13 cents per bushel higher with November up 9-1/2 at $6.98-1/2.
